A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SCAN and contain 39 pages, including Appendices A–D. Text comparison and rendering establish that pages 2–39 are identical; page 1 differs only in the resource link and arXiv stamp. No material gaps prevent comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original judge-accuracy experiments, evaluations of 21 LLMs, and human assessments of generated queries, including Tables 2, 4–9.

after.justification: v4 retains the same original judge-accuracy experiments, 21-model evaluation, ablations, and human query-quality results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: TaxBuilder, RealMix, the visualization and analysis tools, and PC2 evaluation retain identical procedures and components. Sections 2 and 4, Algorithm 1, and the appendix prompts are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same six-domain SCAN-D-V0 coverage, SCAN-HPD, RewardBench-v2, and RMB helpfulness subset. No evaluated task, domain, or test scenario changes.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator sets are identical: naive pointwise evaluation and the direct, single-model, and diverse-model decomposition variants in Table 2, plus the same naive comparator in Table 4.

E3.justification: The 3,343-query evaluation, 636-sample SCAN-HPD dataset, 21 evaluated models, Best-of-N procedures, decoding settings, and human-assessment protocol are unchanged in Appendices B and C.

E4.justification: Both retain the model-combination, model-count, and model-order ablations in Tables 5–7, GPT-OSS capability analyses in Section 6.2, contamination analysis in Appendix C.4.2, and evaluation examples in Appendix D.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is identical, including point estimates and per-rater counts in Table 9. No repeated-run or seed information, uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results match. For example, Table 2 retains Deepseek-R1 accuracies of 0.5694 for naive evaluation and 0.6962 for PC2; Table 8 retains GPT-OSS-120B's overall score of 242.24 and first-place ranking.

T1.justification: The node-insertion relation and evaluation formulations in Equations 1–4 are identical. No mathematical definition, assumption, derivation, or proof changes.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about comprehensive fine-grained capability assessment, PC2 judging accuracy, and insights from evaluating 21 LLMs.

C2.justification: Interpretations of GPT-OSS capability variation and the benefits of fine-grained diagnosis are unchanged. Both retain the limitations concerning multimodal support and evaluation dimensions such as safety, honesty, factuality, and fairness.

D1.justification: The abstract changes the resource destination from liudan193.github.io/Feedbacker/ to github.com/liudan193/SCAN. This revises access information; the PDFs do not establish a change in available code or data. Implementation details and prompts otherwise remain identical.

R1.justification: The references, related-work discussion in Section 7, and positioning against prior benchmarks and EvalTree in Appendix A.1 are identical.

P1.justification: Only the abstract's URL text and first-page arXiv stamp change, from v3 dated 6 October 2025 to v4 dated 1 May 2026. The title, authors, prose, section order, and appendix structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures, tables, captions, placement, and page layout are unchanged. Pages 2–39 render identically, and the first-page link and stamp substitutions do not reorganize its layout.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, empirical evidence, explanations, limitations, and visual presentation are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. The resource-link replacement and updated arXiv stamp do not establish a meaningful overall quality difference; the PDFs provide no evidence of improved resource availability.
